derived_results.claim: The 9-state lead that shrinks the I=1 scale to three states with H=48 and delayed T≈700 is too close to beta=0.10 for the current min-marginal Clopper-Pearson + binary-KL transport certification route.
derived_results.details: Using 6000 paths/candidate/anchor, one-sided CP delta=1e-8 and beta_transport=0.09, adaptive coverage stalled on the high-variance part of the exact KL=1 level. At Q variance r=4.5052414958 and offset x=15, early/late fail counts were 595/484 and min CP upper was 0.10198; at r≈3.7961,x=16 the better-neighbor CP upper was ≈0.09976. A beta_transport=0.09 anchor therefore has no usable KL radius there.
derived_results.scope: This rejects the present certification route as efficient evidence for H=48; it does not prove the H=48 detector's true pair-failure probability exceeds 0.10, because min marginal failure is only an upper bound on joint pair failure.

derived_results.claim: The current I=1 scale {T0=256,g=16,H=64,b=16} is randomized-continuum-certified over the complete exact Gaussian KL=1 level and all 17 discrete offsets under the r73 CP + binary-KL transport method.
derived_results.scope: Exact KL=1 level only; float64 root/merge coverage, not interval-arithmetic machine verification; discrete-time step changes.

derived_results.claim: The current I=0.25 scale {T0=1024,g=64,H=192,b=16} is randomized-continuum-certified over the complete exact Gaussian KL=0.25 level and all 65 discrete offsets under the same method.
derived_results.scope: Exact KL=0.25 level only; float64 root/merge coverage, not interval-arithmetic machine verification; discrete-time step changes.

derived_results.claim: Together with r73's I=0.5 certificate, all three current 10-state bank scales now have exact-KL-level continuum evidence under one common randomized certification construction.
derived_results.statement: I=1 uses H=64, I=0.5 uses H=96, and I=0.25 uses H=192. This aligns the evidence method across scales but still does not prove coverage for every Q with KL above each floor.

exact_next_action: Start radial certification from the I=1 high-variance endpoint, where H=48 was hardest and H=64 has substantial margin. Parameterize Q by variance ratio and KL radius beyond I=1; test a direct joint-pair failure surface and the KL-transport geometry to determine whether one exact-level shell can certify an outward neighborhood. If no global monotonicity is provable, build adaptive radial shells until either a finite cover reaches a high-KL region where an analytic tail lower bound takes over or a counterexample appears. In parallel rerun the existing exact-level coverage roots with interval/directed-rounding arithmetic.
